item.title: README
item.description: Rebuilds Obsidian recipe notes from FastFoto scans using macOS Vision OCR and USDA nutrition.Originals in FastFoto/1980s_reciepes and FastFoto/1990s_reciepes are never modified. Upright copies go to FastFoto/rotated/{era}/ and are embedded in each note.Duplex rotation (portrait FastFoto scans of landscape index cards): _a front = 90° clockwise, _b back = 270° clockwise (90° CCW / front + 180). Same long-edge flip as a typical ADF duplex scan. Pair/rotate/rebuild use this rule; do not reuse per-image OCR rotation for the display JPEGs.cd /Users/mattwatier/Repo/Recipe python3 -m venv .venv source .venv/bin/activate pip install -r Scripts/requirements.txt xcrun swiftc -O -o Scripts/bin/ocr_vision Scripts/ocr_vision.swift \ -framework Vision -framework AppKit -framework Foundation Put USDA_API_KEY= in Scripts/.env (gitignored). Never commit that file or paste the key into notes/README.Unprocessed notes live in Recipes/_Inbox/ as RAW OCR + source card images only (tiny YAML with kaper + card_id). Meal folders (Breakfast, Mains, Sides, Desserts, Drinks, Condiments) are for after processing. Mains have a major protein; Sides are vegetables, starches, and small-bite snacks. Edit the RAW OCR in _Inbox against the card photos. Move a note into Recipes/_Outbox/ when you want it turned into a recipe. Run: python Scripts/process_outbox.py The processor: reads RAW OCR from the note (plain text or markdown; sidecar only if that section is missing; does not re-OCR) reconstructs a full recipe (Scripts/reconstruct.py): # / ## / **Serves:** are headings/metadata; ingredients inside directions are pulled out only if that food is not already listed (loose name match; prefer the Ingredients-section entry; keep the richer amount); a verb line plus a following list is one step; all stated bake/simmer/sauté times are summed into duration ({n}m); steps with no time get a typical duration. Clock times stay out of the step note. Overnight is never invented unless the card says so. Kaper YAML has no markdown; step titles are short actions and notes are instruction sentences writes a Kaper fenced block plus cooking frontmatter (type, course, era from card_id, servings, times, oven, allergens) estimates calories and macros per serving via the USDA API leaves RAW OCR and image embeds intact renames the file to the card’s recipe title when OCR has a clear title files the finished note into the matching meal folder. Mains have a major protein; Sides are vegetables, starches, and small-bite snacks. Breakfast, drinks, desserts, and condiments stay their own folders. Empty outbox is a no-op. Idempotent: a second run with nothing in _Outbox does nothing.Leave RAW OCR untouched. Markdown # / ## / **Serves:** are headings, not ingredients. Pull ingredients out of instructions; reconstruct card shorthand. Only add a direction-derived ingredient if that food is not already in the ingredient list. Match loosely on the food name (ignore amount, unit, prep note, and minor OCR spelling). Prefer the Ingredients-section entry; if one mention is quantified and the other is not, keep the richer amount. Sum all stated step times into duration ({n}m); infer typical times when missing. Clock times do not stay in the step note. Overnight is never invented unless the card says so.Kaper YAML cannot contain markdown. Strip **, #, _, backticks, and list markers from titles, notes, ingredient names, and tags. Leave markdown in ## RAW OCR.Kaper steps: title is a short action, optionally numbered (1. Steam, 2. Poach, 3. Combine & Garnish). note is a full instruction sentence. Clock times go in duration only. Keep qualitative doneness in the note (until tender, till fragrant, reduce by half). Optional tip: for extras such as internal temperature. Do not repeat whole-ingredient amounts in the instruction (Steam broccoli, not Steam 2 heads of broccoli); keep amounts only when subdividing. Cooking tools (dutch oven, buttered pan, mixing bowl) stay in the instruction, never the ingredient list. Encoding: Scripts/parse.py, Scripts/reconstruct.py (shape_step), Scripts/notes.emit_kaper. Reshape existing notes with python Scripts/rebuild_from_ocr.py --cleanup-steps.Kaper amount: is a whole number or decimal only — never a fraction. Unicode and ASCII fractions in RAW OCR (½ ¼ ¾ ⅓ ⅔ ⅛ 1/2 1/4 3/4, mixed 1½, fraction-slash 1⁄2) must become floats in YAML (amount: 0.5 or .5). The fraction glyph must not remain in name (including a leading ⁄2 after 1 was parsed separately).Kaper unit: is not part of name. Size words, kitchen measures, and weights all count. Recognize OCR aliases, then canonicalize: Size / count: small, medium, large, whole, clove, can, stick Volume: cups / c. → cup; tsp / t. / t → tsp; Tb / T. / T / tbsp / tablespoon → tbsp; pint → pt; quart → qt; pinch, dash, pkg Weight: lbs / lb / pounds / # → lb; grams / g / gms → g; oz / ounces → oz A # after an amount is pounds (2# beef → unit: lb), not a markdown heading.Kaper prep/knife directions belong in note, not in name. Match case-insensitively, including OCR near-misses. Canonical vocabulary: halve, quarter, wedge, chunk, rough chop, chop, fine chop, large dice, medium dice, small dice, mince, slice, thin slice, rings, strips, julienne, chiffonade, crush, smash, mince to a paste.Example — OCR ½ small onion, peeled and chopped → amount: 0.5, unit: small, name: onion, note: peeled and chopped. Wrong: amount: 1, name: ⁄2 small onion. Example — OCR 2 cloves garlic, minced → amount: 2, unit: clove, name: garlic, note: minced. Amount/unit/note parsing lives in Scripts/parse.py (parse_amount, split_amount_unit_name, UNIT_ALIASES, _split_note).Do not duplicate ingredients pulled from directions. If onion is already under Ingredients, do not add it again from "sauté the onion". Match loosely on food name (ignore amount/unit/prep and minor OCR spelling). Prefer the Ingredients-section entry; keep the richer amount if only one mention is quantified (Scripts/parse.py: food_names_match, dedupe_ingredients, add_new_ingredients).source .venv/bin/activate python Scripts/pipeline.py --sample # sanity cards first python Scripts/pipeline.py --all # every unique stem OCR text is written once to Scripts/ocr_raw/{card_id}.txt with === FRONT === / === BACK === markers, and copied into a visible RAW OCR section on each note. Existing sidecars are not overwritten on import unless you pass --force-ocr. After that, the note wins. Edit the RAW OCR section in the recipe note (not the sidecar). Exact heading and format: ## RAW OCR ``` ...card text... ``` Rebuild the Kaper form + derived frontmatter from that text (keeps the current folder/filename): python Scripts/rebuild_from_ocr.py python Scripts/rebuild_from_ocr.py --card 1980s_reciepes_0002 Rebuild does not re-OCR unless you pass --reocr. It reads ## RAW OCR first (sidecar fallback if the section is missing), then: replaces the kaper fenced block (including title) updates derived frontmatter: servings, times, oven, nutrition, allergens, tags, course/cuisine never overwrites the RAW OCR section syncs Scripts/ocr_raw/{card_id}.txt from the note so the sidecar stays aligned keeps the existing filename, kaper id, card_id, era, card_sides, status, and rotated image footer Notes with status: reviewed are skipped (Kaper/frontmatter unchanged) unless you pass --force.python Scripts/rebuild_from_ocr.py --all python Scripts/rebuild_from_ocr.py --status ocr-draft python Scripts/rebuild_from_ocr.py --migrate-ocr # visible ## RAW OCR only; no Kaper rebuild Optional OCR refresh (destructive to human sidecar edits only with --force-ocr):python Scripts/rebuild_from_ocr.py --reocr # Vision OCR for missing cache; sidecars stay write-once python Scripts/rebuild_from_ocr.py --reocr --force-ocr # overwrite sidecars from new OCR; notes still win unless RAW OCR is missing python Scripts/pipeline.py --all --skip-ocr # reuse sidecars + cache; still rotate if needed python Scripts/pipeline.py --nutrition-only Notes are keyed by card_id. Re-runs update existing files instead of duplicating them.
